Question: Who runs NHS hospitals in Scotland, how can a patient complain, what are the complaint stages and response times, and what time limits apply?
NHS hospitals in Scotland are run by the relevant NHS health board. A patient can complain by speaking to staff, contacting the NHS health board by phone, email or online, or writing to the relevant NHS organisation; the complaint process starts with staff or a senior member/Feedback and Complaints Officer, and a full response should come within 20 working days at the investigation stage. Time limits are normally 6 months from the event or from when you found out you had reason to complain, but no more than 12 months after the event itself.

Question: What does section 17 say about the time limit for personal injury actions in Scotland, including when it starts? Quote the key words.
Section 17 says that, subject to subsection (3) and section 19A, an action for personal injuries must be commenced “within a period of 3 years” after the relevant date. That starts either from “the date on which the injuries were sustained” (or when a continuing act or omission ceased, if later) or, if later, from when the pursuer became, or could reasonably have become, aware of the specified facts. It also says time under legal disability is disregarded.
